sources.entry: Core Data Editor - Core Data Editor lets you easily view, edit and analyze applications‘ data. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/luin/medis) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Core Data Editor is a Mac app for viewing, editing and analyzing the Core Data stores of Mac and iOS applications.
summary.what_it_does: Core Data Editor lets you view, edit and analyze the data of Mac and iOS applications that use Core Data. According to the README it supports XML, SQLite and binary stores and visualizes all relationships between objects. You can edit data and generate Objective-C code for the data model. The README describes the internal architecture: a managed objects view controller shows objects from an entity or from a relationship in a table, with a search field for filtering and controls to add or remove objects. Data coordinator classes (subclasses of CDERequestDataCoordinator) handle loading, table columns, editing, and saving column layout for entity, to-one, unordered and ordered relationship cases. The app includes a first-launch setup walkthrough that can be skipped.
use_cases: inspect the contents of a Core Data SQLite store
edit records in an app's local database for debugging
visualize entity relationships in a Core Data model
generate Objective-C code from a data model
browse objects of a Core Data app on Mac
filter and manage managed objects in a table view
notable: Supports XML, SQLite and binary Core Data stores
Visualizes all relationships between managed objects
Generates Objective-C code for the data model
Architecture split into data coordinator subclasses for entity, to-one, to-many and ordered relationships
Optional guided setup on first launch
caveats: The README gives no release downloads or binary installation; running it requires building from source in Xcode
The README does not state supported macOS or Xcode versions
Build status badges are empty in the README, so current build health is unclear
